newsitem.title: UK: Bookies tip more Grand National bets after delay.
newsitem.headline: Bookies tip more Grand National bets after delay.

text.p: Britain's betting shops said on Monday they expected even more punters to bet on the nation's most famous steeplechase, the Grand National, after it was postponed for 48 hours by a bomb alert.

Last year the industry turned over about 60 million pounds ($98 million at current rates) but this time it could reach 85 million, said Malcolm Palmer, public relations manager at bookmakers Coral, owned by brewers Bass.
"There are not many cancelling and there are opportunities now for a lot more to put a bet on today," said Palmer.
The industry had predicted wagers of 70 million pounds but this should easily be exceeded by the time the race is run at 1600 GMT on Monday, he said.
"There is no great indication of people wanting to cancel their bets," said Graham Sharpe, media relations manager of Brent Walker Group's 1,700-branch William Hill chain.
The Grand National is the single most important date in the betting calendar for the industry, which obtains about 10 percent of its total annual income from the one horse race alone.
The event is watched by 400 million people world-wide and 15 million adults in Britain, or about one third of the adult population, have a bet every year.

"It does give plenty of people another bite at the cherry. So I think we will see a few more bets being placed today," said Ed Nicholson, public relations manager at Ladbroke Group, Britain's largest chain of betting outlets.
The bookmakers are hoping that a rank outsider wins, unlike last year, when favourite Rough Quest romped home at odds of 7-1.

Ladbrokes, which has taken a single 20,000 pound bet on Wylde Hide each way at 16-1, stands to lose some 500,000 pounds if the horse wins. The firm is also holding another 10,000 pound stake to win on the same horse.

Ladbrokes has also taken a 20 pound double bet on one of the favourites, Suny Bay, to win the National and John Major to win the May 1 British election from a punter who reasoned that they are both "grey".
The race is widely viewed as the most open for many years with a number of horses in with a good chance of winning. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
